arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Paul Clement argued Arizona bears disproportionate costs from illegal immigration.
Clement stated Arizona borrowed federal standards for its own enforcement.
Clement claimed the state enlisted resources for uniform federal laws.
Clement criticized the government's theory on ad hoc versus systematic enforcement.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Arizona argues it bears high costs from illegal immigration. The state wants to use federal standards for enforcement. It seeks to enlist state resources for uniform laws. The United States argues immigration status is a federal matter. It claims state enforcement violates federal exclusivity. The dispute centers on state versus federal power.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between state and federal police power. It determines who controls immigration enforcement at the border. It shapes how states interact with federal immigration laws. It impacts daily interactions between police and residents. It clarifies the scope of state sovereignty in this area.
